{{Quote|Like Lothal, my home planet of Chandrila is suffering at the hands of the Empire. But if we help these two worlds, what of Onderon, or Ryloth, or Montross?|[[Mon Mothma]]|<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion">{{Rebels|In the Name of the Rebellion}}</ref>}}
'''Montross'''<ref name="Skystrike Academy" /> was a [[planet]]<ref name="Build XWing 15">{{BuildXWingCite|15|Starfighter Aces}}</ref> in the [[Binary star system|binary star]]<ref name="The Antilles Extraction" /> [[Montross system]] in the [[Truum sector]] of the [[Mid Rim Territories]].<ref name="Appendix" /> By [[2 BBY]],<ref name="HC-57 Date">{{HelmetCollectionCite|57|Highlights of the Saga}} dates the events of the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' episode "[[The Antilles Extraction]]" to [[2 BBY]].</ref> Montross had fallen under the control of the [[Galactic Empire]], which established [[Skystrike Academy]], an elite [[Imperial Academy|flight academy]] for future [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot|TIE fighter pilots]], in its [[atmosphere]].<ref name="The Antilles Extraction" /> The [[Vaathkree Trade Corridor]] connected Montross to the celestial bodies [[Contruum]] and [[Gizer]].<ref name="Vaathkree" />

{{Planet-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
Montross first appeared unnamed in "[[The Antilles Extraction]]," the third episode of the [[canon]] animated series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''{{'}} [[Star Wars Rebels Season Three|third season]], which first aired on [[October 8]], [[2016]]. Montross was identified in the [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] entry for Skystrike Academy, released on [[October 10]].

The name itself has existed since the earliest drafts of what would become [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]: in the first rough draft of [[May]] [[1974]], [[Montross (Aquilae)|Montross]] was an [[aide]] to [[General]] [[Luke Skywalker (The Star Wars)|Skywalker]] on [[Aquilae (The Star Wars)|Aquilae]]; in the second draft, Montross Holdaack was the friendly science officer on [[Han Solo]]'s ship who helps Solo and [[Chewbacca]] fake a reactor overload to commandeer the ship; in the third and fourth drafts he is relegated to an adversarial role, becoming akin to [[Greedo]] in the former and an Imperial bureaucrat in charge of [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]] in the latter.<ref name="Making">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> Actor [[Richard LeParmentier]] was originally considered for that part, but the role of Montross was ultimately cut from the script, and LeParmentier received the role of Admiral [[Conan Antonio Motti|Motti]] instead.<ref name="Coup">{{InsiderCite|Special Edition 2014|A Certain Point of View|A Certain Point of View: The Death Star Coup}}</ref>

In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, the name was used in [[Star Wars: Jango Fett: Open Seasons|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'']] and ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]'', written by [[W. Haden Blackman|Haden Blackman]], tie-ins to [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], as the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Montross (bounty hunter)|Montross]], voiced by [[Clancy Brown]].
